approval_required_for: Conditional only: if the current identity document, cited Vivado export facts, and authorized simulator executable records provide multiple conflicting mappings that prevent a unique hash-bound compile plan, obtain bounded approval selecting among explicitly cited candidates. Such approval cannot substitute for evidence or authorize changes to the wrapper/source hashes, checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, numeric policy, tolerance, or golden outputs.

consumes: current board identity document and source_identity_sha256
current user-supplied sample-project wrapper and complete source hash inventory
current Vivado export provenance/facts referenced by the identity document
current tool_profile and authorized simulator executable records
current numeric comparison policy and resolved tolerances
executable_actions.on_failure: Retain the board-layer verification-capability blocker and all SACG trust barriers. Do not guess a wrapper top, Vivado export context, executable, source hash, or authority reference. If cited evidence yields conflicting candidate mappings rather than a unique hash-bound mapping, request bounded human approval identifying the cited alternatives; otherwise repair only the missing harness/protocol capability. Do not run VCS acceptance, alter RTL, regenerate golden outputs, or change tolerance.
produces: verification/board_simulation/board_simulation_manifest.json with a content hash binding the current identity document
verification/board_simulation/canonical_vcs_compile_plan.json with compile_authority and per-command authority_refs bound to cited Vivado export facts
executable_actions.rationale: The first failed gate is an exact-board simulation identity and compile-authority binding failure. A bounded manifest/harness repair is required before a real hardware trace can be trusted. This action changes only candidate verification binding metadata and command authorization; it must preserve the exact user-supplied wrapper/source hashes, generated semantic-testbench contract/hash, checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, and numeric policy.

consumes: current user-supplied sample-project wrapper and complete source hash inventory
generated semantic testbench and recorded hash
immutable numeric comparison policy and resolved tolerances
executable_actions.on_failure: If compilation, elaboration, expected-output binding, tensor-consumption instrumentation, or trace collection fails, classify it as a current verification-capability/harness failure and return to bounded current-layer repair without a hardware correctness claim. If real RTL/tool evidence reports a protocol, value, order, liveness, or frontier failure, run repair.localize_current_board_failure before any wrapper/runtime/RTL patch. Do not reopen lower layers or advance to board closure.
produces: verification/debug_closure/boundary_trace.json with board core-start, ingress, egress, ordering, and lifecycle/frontier observations
verification/board_simulation/rtl_output.memh and comparison evidence when simulation completes
executable_actions.rationale: After case_axi_ddr_interface passes, the required next current-layer action is a real board-wrapped VCS replay with boundary trace and diagnostics. The replay must establish the earliest board causal boundary, if any, using the exact wrapper and immutable semantic inputs rather than a simplified test shell or RTL-derived expected data.

consumes: passing real VCS replay report, trace, and diagnostics
exact wrapper and testbench source-hash records
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board_axi_ddr_closure failed and invoke current-layer causal localization using the fresh trace. Treat missing target-model reference execution, complete Transformer-block tensor catalog/hash coverage, bound loader consumption, numeric policy, or semantic evidence as a verification-capability failure, not hardware correctness. Treat real protocol/value/order/liveness evidence as a board integration failure. In either case, do not change checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, tolerance, golden boundary, exact wrapper, or source hashes and do not promote.
produces: fresh DDR image roundtrip gate report
fresh Stage7 candidate real-tool evidence set for board_axi_ddr_closure
executable_actions.rationale: A passing VCS replay alone is insufficient. The remaining current-layer gates must prove AXI protocol behavior, DDR image/order correctness, no pipeline deadlock, multilayer functional semantics, immutable numeric comparison, and complete in-scope weight consumption before the board layer can receive fresh semantic evidence.

consumes: fresh VCS functional report and analyzer diagnosis
fresh deadlock/AXI diagnostic report when available
current board simulation manifest and compile-plan authority evidence
executable_actions.on_failure: If the trace lacks direct core-start, ingress, egress, named causal-boundary, and current-certificate evidence, retain localization at the board wrapper/harness boundary and prohibit lower-layer backtrack. If no fresh failure exists, mark this action not applicable rather than fabricating a localization record. Any proposed implementation change must be confined to the localized board integration slice and rerun the same board layer before promotion.
produces: verification/debug_closure/current_layer_causal_repair_context.json identifying the earliest observed board boundary or capability gap
bounded current-layer repair request or a hash-bound lower-layer contradiction record when and only when the required contradiction evidence exists
executable_actions.rationale: This action is required only if the fresh board replay or its follow-on gates fail. It converts actual tool evidence into a bounded earliest-causal repair context. A board output/lifecycle-frontier symptom is not by itself a lower-kernel failure and independent AXI/prefetch progress is not output-frontier progress.

consumes: all fresh reports produced by the preceding board binding repair, replay, gate-completion, and conditional localization actions

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep all active barriers and retry requests effective, leave backend/board-runtime promotion blocked, and preserve the new failure/localization evidence for the next bounded repair loop. produces: fresh Stage7 retry submission decision referencing only newly hash-bound reports
updated artifact-trust status retaining rejected artifacts as planning/debug evidence until a verified Stage7 outcome exists

observations: The current board layer has an executed failure only at real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface. Its concrete blockers are provenance/authorization bindings for simulation.source_identity_sha256, compile_authority, ordered-command authority_refs, and simulator executables; this is a verification harness and tool-protocol failure, not evidence of an RTL, AXI, DDR, memory-layout, or numerical defect.

functional_sim is failed as a dependency-blocked aggregate gate: case_vcs_functional_sim, the VCS analyzer, deadlock/AXI analysis, multilayer functional, protocol, DDR roundtrip, and board semantic-evidence tools were not run. The absent board semantic-evidence report is consequently an evidence gap, not proof that the existing target reference, tolerance, loader, or DUT values are wrong.

The current hierarchy records all operator-leaf and connected single-transformer-layer gates as pass. The live certificates and timing evidence preserve target-model semantics and the elastic variable-latency kernel invariant: 13 boundary orders and required cross-token overlap are certified, while strict same-cycle completion is not required. No current trace challenges these certificates.

No boundary failure, failing transaction trace, root module, or output/lifecycle-frontier symptom has been produced for the board layer. The CCTG closure explicitly requires verification-capability repair before requesting a hardware boundary trace. Independent AXI or prefetch progress must not be treated as output/lifecycle progress when replay becomes available.

sacg_memory_truth has 16 active scoped contamination barriers and six open retry requests for board_axi_ddr_closure. They keep rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts as planning/debug evidence only and block downstream consumption or promotion. There are no open scoped backtrack requests. Older barrier labels involving board-interface discovery or multilayer pipeline do not independently reopen those currently passing gates; their rejected artifact lineages remain untrusted.

No retry_reconciliation_contract was supplied. Therefore no active retry request or contamination barrier may be silently superseded or cleared by this decision; a fresh Stage7 result and SACG status update are required. The conditional design-team router returned no_split, which adds no specialist evidence or alternative repair path.
proposed_actions: Rebuild only the board simulation manifest/compile-plan binding from the already discovered exact board identity, current Vivado export facts, allowed tool profile, wrapper/source hash inventory, and immutable semantic contract; do not modify the wrapper, checkpoint, target reference, stimulus, golden output, testbench contract, or tolerance.
Rerun case_axi_ddr_interface first. Only after it passes, execute the exact board-wrapped VCS targeted replay with boundary monitoring, target-model comparison inputs, and AXI/deadlock diagnostics.

If the replay passes basic functional execution, complete the remaining board gate DAG in dependency order and assemble board semantic evidence proving independent expected outputs, numeric comparison, data order, and complete in-scope weight consumption.

If a current replay fails, localize its earliest causal board boundary using the emitted trace before proposing any code change. Keep lower layers closed unless the trace directly contradicts a named certified invariant with required core/ingress/egress/certificate bindings.

Record the fresh retry outcome against the active SACG barriers and open Stage7 retry requests. Do not promote to backend, implementation, bitstream, runtime ABI, or board runtime unless every required board gate passes with fresh real-tool evidence.
risks: Model/numeric risk: the board replay must use the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, independent target-model expected outputs, generated semantic-testbench hashes, and unchanged resolved comparison policy/tolerances. DUT output must never set or loosen the tolerance.

Weight/data-order risk: board-level acceptance still lacks executed proof that the board loader/harness consumed every required Transformer-block tensor from the complete-scope catalog in the intended runtime order. Embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain outside the DUT and outside this weight/golden scope.

Integration risk: an identity or compile-plan repair that substitutes a simplified wrapper, uncited Vivado export, guessed hierarchy, or unauthorized executable would evade rather than repair the exact-board requirement.

Runtime/liveness risk: until the real replay runs, no claim can be made about AXI protocol, DDR image mapping, transfer counts, deadlock, input acceptance, core lifecycle start, output frontier, or output validity.

Hierarchy risk: reopening leaf modules or the connected kernel without a current hash-bound direct contradiction would discard live certified knowledge and violate the mandatory three-layer repair loop.

Artifact-trust risk: historical and current rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts are contaminated for downstream acceptance; only newly generated reports from the repaired binding and ordered reruns may support a retry decision.
